chunks: 306 - A group of scholars narrated to me, from al-Talaqbari, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Abu al-Hasan al-Balkhi, from Ahmad ibn Mabandar al-Iskafi, from al-Ala' al-Nadari, from al-Hasan ibn Shammun, who said:
I read this letter to Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him), in his own handwriting: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

O Ali, may Allah grant you a good reward, and settle you in His Paradise, and keep away the degradation of the world and the Hereafter from you, and may Allah raise you with us. O Ali, I have tested you and gained experience with you in well-wishing, obedience, and service, and in reverence and fulfilling what is obligatory upon you. If I say that I have not seen your like, I hope I would be truthful. May Allah reward you with the Gardens of Firdous as a dwelling. Your position and your service in heat and cold, in night and day, have not been hidden from me. I ask Allah, when He gathers the creatures for the Resurrection, to love you with a mercy that you will delight in. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing of the supplication.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِي: Abu Ja'far al-Thani, referring to Imam al-Jawad (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مَابَنْدَارَ الْإِسْكَافِي: Ahmad ibn Mabandar al-Iskafi, a narrator
key_terms.التَّلْعَكْبَرِيُّ: Al-Talaqbari, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.جَنَّاتِ الْفِرْدَوْسِ: The Gardens of Firdous (highest level of Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Jawad say about Ali ibn Mahziyar's service and character?
ai.summary: This authentic letter from Imam al-Jawad (AS) to his trusted emissary Ali ibn Mahziyar highlights the critical role of the 'Approved Emissaries' (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'a) in maintaining communication between the Hidden Imam and the Shia community during the Minor Occultation. The Imam’s personal endorsement of Ali’s unwavering service in both ease and hardship underscores the scholarly tradition of valuing reliable deputies who preserve religious authority and guidance. This praise serves as a model for future scholars and leaders, emphasizing that consistent devotion and piety are essential for spiritual leadership.
